record.entity_title: Red-White-Red Card for skilled workers in shortage occupations (third-country)
record.fact_text: As a non-EU (third-country) national you may apply for a Red-White-Red Card as a Skilled Worker in a Shortage Occupation, valid for 24 months; the shortage-occupation route requires a binding job offer at the legally stipulated minimum pay and reaching at least 55 of 100 points on the eligibility criteria.
record.evidence_quote: As a third-country citizen, you may apply for a Red-White-Red Card as a Skilled Worker in a Shortage Occupation valid for 24 months

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any job offer lets a non-EU worker move to Austria. Actually: the Red-White-Red Card is points-based (min. 55/100) and the shortage-occupation route needs a job on the annual shortage list at the minimum pay. Action required: check the current shortage-occupation list and your score before planning the move.

record.entity_title: EU/EEA/Swiss citizen: apply for an EU residence document for stays over 3 months
record.fact_text: As a citizen of an EU/EEA country or Switzerland you must apply for an EU residence document if you stay in Denmark for more than 3 months, and you must apply before the three months expire (jobseekers have up to 6 months); Nordic citizens do not need one.
record.evidence_quote: Citizens of EU, EEA countries and Switzerland have to apply for an EU residence document if they stay for more than 3 months.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an EU citizen just moves to Denmark with no paperwork. Actually: for stays over three months you must apply for an EU residence document (registration certificate) before the three months expire; note Nordic citizens are exempt. Action required: apply to SIRI in Copenhagen soon after arrival.

record.entity_title: Pay Limit Scheme: residence and work permit for a high-salary job (third-country)
record.fact_text: As a non-EU/EEA national offered a job in Denmark with a high salary you can apply for a residence and work permit under the Pay Limit Scheme; the salary must be at least the annually-regulated minimum amount (DKK 552,000 per year in 2026).
record.evidence_quote: You have been offered a job in Denmark with a salary of DKK 552,000 or higher.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any job offer qualifies a non-EU worker for a Danish permit. Actually: the widely-used Pay Limit Scheme requires a salary at or above an annually-set minimum (DKK 552,000 in 2026), regardless of your field or hours. Action required: check the offered salary against the current minimum amount.
